overall_summary: Space and exoplanet content, particularly first-person 'What If' survival scenarios and extreme planetary environments (e.g., burning ice, liquid diamonds, supersonic rubies), are the primary growth drivers for the channel. Conversely, passive psychology facts and basic animal trivia consistently underperform, indicating that the audience craves high-stakes, visually rich cosmic mysteries.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' achieved 970 views, and 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' secured 952 views with 38 likes, showing the highest viewer retention and engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on first-person perspective survival scenarios on extreme cosmic bodies, utilizing the 'What If You Fell Into...' framing.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring extreme physical contrasts or high-value imagery such as 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,055 views) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views) vastly outperform abstract space topics.
winning_patterns.action: Craft hooks around tangible, extreme materials (rubies, diamonds, iron, glass) and physical oxymorons to instantly capture visual interest.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' struggled to exceed 53 views across multiple uploads, and 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' stalled at 38 views.
weak_patterns.action: Phase out standard cognitive psychology facts unless they can be re-framed as a high-stakes horror/mystery micro-story.

next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into the Iron Rain Planet?
next_video.opening_direction: Show a close-up of molten metal droplets melting through a spacesuit visor with the hook: 'If you fell into WASP-76b, you wouldn't just burn—you'd be pelted by liquid iron rain.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the planet's winds blow at 11,000 miles per hour, turning the molten iron rain into supersonic metallic bullets that shred anything in seconds.
next_video.reason: Combines the highly successful 'What If You Fell Into...' narrative structure with extreme planetary weather (molten iron rain), matching the 21-second sweet spot of previous high-performing shorts.

experiment: Test a 21-second 'What If' survival scenario focused on deep-sea extreme environments (e.g., falling to the bottom of the Mariana Trench) to see if the high-performing cosmic survival format translates successfully to oceanography.
